chapter one

The story

StatementFounderPillarsMission & vision

1.1 Statement

Every Lakira saree is handpicked — made for her, chosen with power. Tradition, worn the way she lives today.

1.2 The founder

Lakshmi Ramachandra

“We warmly invite you to celebrate the new chapter of Lakira Couture with us.”

From the Grand Opening invitation, signed by Lakshmi Ramachandra.

16·10·26Grand opening
RR Nagar80 Feet Road, 5th Stage
MysoreSilk and crepe at the heart

1.3 Four pillars

What Lakira stands for

i.

Handpicked

Every saree is chosen by hand, one at a time. Fewer pieces, each one worth the drape.

ii.

Heritage weaves

Mysore silk, Mysore crepe, hand-painted silks and temple zari borders — crafts with a story.

iii.

Tradition, today

“Tradition meets contemporary fashion”: heirloom craft, styled for the way she lives now.

iv.

Styled for her

Our team helps each customer choose the saree, the blouse and the look — not just the price.

1.4 Mission

To bring handpicked heritage sarees to the women of Bengaluru, and help each one choose a drape that feels like her.

Vision

To be the saree house women trust for every chapter of their life — the first silk, the wedding, the heirloom.

Draft Mission and vision are written from the logo taglines and posts. Confirm the wording with Lakshmi.

chapter two

The mark

AnatomyTaglinesVersionsSpace & sizePlacementMisuse

2.1 Anatomy

A miniature painting, not a logo

The Lakira mark is an illustration in the style of an Indian miniature. Treat it like artwork: give it a frame, a light ground and plenty of room.

123456
  1. 1

    Mughal arch and lotus

    A palace window frames everything. Re-use the arch for photos (see chapter v).

  2. 2

    The painted L

    Four panels, like four swatches of woven silk, in blue, rose, leaf green and coral.

  3. 3

    Her

    A woman in a rose saree — the customer as the heroine of the brand.

  4. 4

    Parrots and blossoms

    Borrowed from miniature paintings: joy, beauty and courtship.

  5. 5

    LAKIRA

    A classic serif in warm brown, with a sweeping K and R.

  6. 6

    COUTURE

    Wide-spaced capitals between two small ornaments.

This file was rebuilt from the logo on the hiring poster (upscaled and cleaned). For print, ask the designer for the original high-resolution artwork.

2.2 Taglines

Two lines are in use

Your posts carry two different taglines under the logo. Choose one as the primary and keep the other for campaigns.

Handpicked sarees

Made for her · Chosen with power

On the Grand Opening invitation and saree posts. Recommended primary — it says what you sell and who it’s for.

Tradition meets

Contemporary fashion

On the hiring post. Use as a campaign line, not under the logo.

2.3 Versions

Full mark, monogram

The illustration loses its detail below about 160 px. For small spaces, use the monogram: the arch and the L, drawn as simple lines.

1 · Full mark on its tile

Default for posts, the store, bags, invitations and the website.

2 · Monogram New

Profile picture, saree tags, favicon, watermarks, stitched labels.

3 · Monogram in zari New

Gold on wine for boxes, ribbons, foil stamping and the reel end card.

The monogram is a new proposal from Core8Media. Approve it with the client before printing.

2.4 Space and size

Room to breathe

xxxx

Keep clear space of x on every side, where x is the height of the “L” in LAKIRA. Nothing — text, photo edges, other logos — goes inside it.

Full mark
min. 160 px wide on screen · 30 mm in print
Monogram
min. 32 px · 8 mm

2.5 Placement

Always on its tile

The painting has soft, light edges. It only works on Ivory, Blush or Paper — on anything darker, keep it inside its ivory tile, the way the “Timeless Craft” post does.

The silk palette

3.1 House colours

Woven, not invented

Every Lakira colour is taken from the store’s own sarees and posts. Four house colours carry the brand; the collection colours change with the saree you are showing. Tap any colour to copy its code.

Collection colours — let the saree lead

3.2 Proportion

Mostly ivory, a touch of zari

55% Ivory & Paper
25% Wine
12% Zari

Ivory gives the silk space. Wine anchors the brand. Zari gold is the jewellery — rules, numerals, ornaments, never big floods. The last sliver belongs to whichever saree is on the post.

chapter five

Zari & motif

Temple borderZari pointerArch frameFabric insetOrnamentPaper

5.1 Building blocks

Borrowed from the loom

Six elements, all taken from your sarees and posts. Use them the same way every time and every post will look like it came from one house.

The temple border

Gopuram teeth over a woven zari band — from the Grand Opening invite. Bottom edge of invitations, banners, boxes and this book.

Rose-dust silk, temple zari

The zari pointer

A white dot on the detail, a hairline down, one line of caption. Your signature on close-up posts.

The arch frame

The palace window from the logo, used to frame portraits and hero photos. Thin gold inner line.

The fabric inset

A white-framed close-up laid over the wider shot — as in your “Mysore Silk” post. One per post.

The lotus ornament

From the top of the logo arch. A divider between headline and details, in Zari Gold.

Grand Opening

Handmade paper

Warm, textured cream for invitations and announcements. Never for product posts — those stay on silk.

vi
chapter six

The lens

Five rulesWhat to avoid

6.1 Photography

The silk is the star

Your close-ups are already the strongest thing on the feed. These five rules keep every shoot looking like them.

01

Dark stone, soft flowers

Lay the saree on dark slate or stone. A small sprig of flowers at the top edge — never more than one corner.

  • Slate, charcoal or dark wood only
  • Flowers in a tone of the saree
02

Go close — the border is the hero

Fill the frame with the zari, the weave or the motif. Shallow focus so the eye lands on the craft.

  • Macro or 50–85 mm lens
  • Focus on the border, let the body blur
03

Warm side light, true colour

One soft light from the side so the zari glints. Colour must match the saree in the store — customers will compare.

  • No flash, no coloured filters
  • Check the colour against the real saree before posting
04

Fold it like a gift

Crisp, even folds with the border running diagonally across the frame. The diagonal is a Lakira habit — keep it.

  • Border on a diagonal, top-right to bottom-left
  • Steam out every crease
05

One photo, one line

Every image gets one short, sensory caption — never a block of text. Story posts can pair a wide shot and a detail on Lakira Wine.

  • Caption in Jost, 1–2 lines
  • Story cards: Cormorant headline + 2 photos
AVOIDHarsh flash and phone-camera HDR
AVOIDCluttered racks or mannequins behind the saree
AVOIDFilters that shift the silk’s true colour
AVOIDCropping off the border or the pallu
AVOIDText or stickers over the zari
vii
chapter seven

The voice

PersonalityYour best linesThe formulaWords

7.1 Personality

A storyteller of silk

Lakira speaks the way a knowledgeable friend talks about a saree she loves: unhurried, sensory and quietly confident.

Sensory

Name the colour, the fabric, the feel: aubergine, Mysore crepe, the weight of zari.

Reverent

Honour the weavers and the craft. Tradition is the story, not a sales word.

Quietly confident

No shouting, no exclamation marks. Let the saree persuade.

Warm

Personal and welcoming, like the invitation: “We warmly invite you…”

7.2 Your best lines

Already written by you

“Where silk becomes a canvas. A hand-painted story, woven into the timeless elegance of Mysore Crepe.”

“The border remembers temple walls — carved once in stone, now woven in zari.”

“Aubergine silk, gold zari, and the weight of tradition.”

The caption formula

Colour+Fabric+One feeling

“Delicate checks, golden zari — understated elegance in Mysore silk.”

Write this

Lilac checks, golden zari — understated elegance in Mysore silk.

Handpicked for the woman who chooses with power.

Come, drape it. Visit us on 80 Feet Road, RR Nagar.

Not this

MEGA SALE!!! 50% OFF ALL SAREES 🔥🔥🔥

Best price in Bangalore, DM for rate.

Same as designer copy, cheap quality available.

Words we love

handpickeddrapepalluzariweaveheirloomMysore silktemple bordertimeless

Words we avoid

cheapsale!!!best pricereplicahurrystock clearance

Always write Lakira Couture in full the first time; “Lakira” alone after that. Never “Lakira Sarees” as the name — it’s Lakira Couture. Captions: English first, a Kannada line is welcome; one emoji at most.

8.1 The feed

A grid with a rhythm

Plan the feed in rows of three, so the profile reads like a lookbook rather than a noticeboard.

DETAIL
FOLD
STORY
DETAIL
FOLD
FESTIVE
DETAIL
FOLD
NEWS
  1. 1
    One saree per row.

    Detail with a zari pointer, then the folded saree — the same colour twice reads as a collection.

  2. 2
    Third tile breaks the pattern.

    A story card on Lakira Wine, a festive greeting, or store news.

  3. 3
    Logo only on story and news tiles.

    Close-ups stay clean. The profile picture already says who you are.

8.2 Post templates

Three posts, endless sarees

Feed posts at 1080 × 1350. Swap the photo and the caption; keep everything else.

8.3 Reels and stories

Keep the logo, captions and the call to action inside the clear area — Instagram covers the shaded parts.
